summary: This continuation plans integral local models from polynomial Schubert closures and minuscule Hodge embeddings to normal scheme representatives, tangent spaces spanned by formal curves, same-residue-field Schubert curves, EL/PEL Drinfeld comparisons and connected geometric tubes. It keeps general-bound v-sheaves separate from minuscule scheme models and records the precise modular-representation, algebraic-loop and cohomological supplier gaps. The independent rational Gelfand commutativity proof receives an exhaustive split brief.

nodes.statement: For the faithful minuscule H-representation ρ₁ of KPZ §3.3.11, whose composed cocharacter over K̃ is minuscule, choose the split Weyl-module Z_p-form H₀↪GL(Λ₀). It gives a closed immersion of the Weil-restricted polynomial BD Grassmannians, and consequently of the bounded closure models, after the appropriate reflex extension. The representation-theoretic input includes uniqueness of stable minuscule lattices up to the representation centralizer, not uniqueness of all stable lattices.

sources.match: Uses highest weights to identify lattices and then proves the BD and model embeddings.

proofSteps: Request the integral minuscule Weyl-lattice and reductive closed-immersion theorems from the integral representation supplier.
Compare Γ-stable and split Weyl lattices via their centralizer.
Construct the torsor map; apply the closed-BD criterion and restrict to schematic generic closures.
acceptance: Repeated isotypic factors allow centralizer changes; a fixed chosen basis is not canonical.

nodes.title: Restriction of structure on local models
nodes.statement: For finite K/F, an O_K-lattice Λ⊂V, and minuscule μ of Res_(K/F)GL(V), the O_F-linear restriction embedding Res_(O_K/O_F)GL(Λ)↪GL(Λ as O_F-module) induces a closed immersion of polynomial local models over O_E. If Λ has O_K-rank n then its O_F-rank is n[K:F]; the μ-rank is the sum of the embedding-wise ranks. This includes ramified K/F.

sources.match: Uses endomorphism-preserving lattices and the finite-flat polynomial map.

proofSteps: Construct the closed group embedding by the O_K-endomorphism equations.
For the polynomial comparison use O_F[v]→O_(K₀)[u], v↦E_K(u)+π_F, and the finite-flat torsor restriction theorem requested at RG2.0a.
The special-fibre flag map is locally closed on the relevant component; ind-properness makes the bounded map proper, and the PZ criterion plus Nakayama makes it a closed immersion.
acceptance: For an extension of degree e and constant rank r over each embedding the total quotient rank is er.

nodes.title: Closed embeddings after a representation power
nodes.statement: For quasi-tame classical G, p>2, and a Hodge representation of the product form of KPZ (3.3.24), a direct sum ρ^(⊕m) admits an O_F-lattice Λ and a quasiparahoric 𝒢′ with (𝒢′)°=𝒢° such that 𝒢′↪GL(Λ) is closed and M^pol_(𝒢,μ)=M^pol_(𝒢′,μ)↪Gr(md,Λ)_(O_E) is closed, with dimensions interpreted for the resulting power. The theorem permits changing the full fixer. If π₁(G)_I is torsion-free, or x is generic in its facet and the adjoint division-algebra obstruction is absent, one can take 𝒢′=𝒢 as in Remark 3.3.26.

sources.match: Composes the embeddings and handles the division-algebra case by unramified descent.

proofSteps: In the unobstructed case compose the three closed model embeddings.
In general pass to a finite unramified field making G quasi-split, choose the Γ-stable generic facet fixer there and use its descended quasiparahoric.
Restrict scalars and sum the lattices. Descend the prescribed model map using schematic density and separatedness.
acceptance: A theorem for the connected component must not be silently promoted to the original full fixer.

nodes.title: The tame symplectic lattice-chain embedding
nodes.statement: For the KP §2.3.1 symplectic Hodge representation over Q_p with p>2, G tamely split, p∤|π₁(G^der)|, x a building point and the constructed toral building maps ι,s satisfying (2.3.2), the integral fixer maps 𝒢_x↪GSp(𝓛)↪GL(𝓛) are closed and induce M^pol_G↪M^pol_(GSp,z)_(O_E)↪M^pol_(GL,y)_(O_E). The polynomial representation must specialize to the actual lattice chain of ι(x); an arbitrary lattice is not substituted.

sources.match: Uses symplectic factorization, polynomial chain representations and the PZ criterion.

proofSteps: Import the symplectic factorization of the toral building map and the polynomial lift of its integral representation. These require the Satake symplectic classification and projective freeness contracts, recorded as supplier gaps. In the unramified splitting decomposition retain the degree m_j of every centralizer division algebra, every Galois twist and the m_j translated lattice-chain copies; otherwise the source representation and its building point have the wrong dimension.
Over the maximal unramified extension verify the neutral-component closure condition (*) in k[[u]].
Apply the PZ criterion and descend closedness and the morphism via flat generic density.
acceptance: The condition (*) is over k[[u]], not a second generic fibre k((u)).

nodes.title: The GL chain incidence model
nodes.statement: For a standard periodic O_F-lattice chain Λ_(i+r)=π_F^(-1)Λ_i in V and the standard minuscule bound of subspace rank d, the GL local model represents rank-d locally direct summands F_i⊂Λ_i⊗R, compatible with all transitions and period identifications. It is the flat closure of the diagonal generic Grassmannian in ∏_(i=0)^(r−1)Gr(d,Λ_i). The equality of the incidence functor and the flat closure includes the GL-chain flatness theorem; incidence equations alone do not establish it.

sources.match: Uses the GL chain functor.
Provides the compatible-chain moduli language.

proofSteps: Construct the closed incidence subfunctor of the finite product of Grassmannians.
Use the requested GL/GSp standard-chain flatness theorem and identify the generic diagonal; then schematic density gives equality with the flat closure.
acceptance: For GL₂ Iwahori and d=1 the special fibre has two projective-line components; it is not a single smooth Grassmannian.

Compares goodness for a chain and its total lattice.

nodes.title: Period-total Grassmannian embedding
nodes.statement: For lattices Λ_i of a finite determining segment and ranks d_i, the direct-sum map ∏Gr(d_i,Λ_i)→Gr(Σd_i,⊕Λ_i) is a closed immersion. Its image is the locus stable under the summand idempotents with the prescribed component ranks. Composing the chain incidence map with this map and the tame symplectic embedding proves KP Corollary 2.3.16. For the polarized total lattice of KP §2.3.15 retain the index range of 2r−1+a terms, its pairing and duality scalings; the target rank is half the total dimension. No argument changes a non-vertex building point into a hyperspecial vertex by just repeating its representation.

sources.match: The total-lattice conclusion needs the product-Grassmannian argument.

sources.locator: Lemma 2.3.1, p. 12; chain variant after Definition 3.4.4, p. 29
sources.match: Uses the corresponding total-chain embedding.

proofSteps: Cut out idempotent stability as closed equations; fixed summand ranks select open-and-closed components in that closed locus.
Recover each summand by the idempotent image, proving the functorial inverse onto the image.
Compose the symplectic, chain-incidence and product embeddings; generic density identifies the composite with the representation-induced map.
acceptance: For two rank 1 summands of rank 2 lattices the target is Gr(2,Λ₀⊕Λ₁); requiring only total rank 2 admits wrong component ranks.

nodes.title: Good embeddings cut out by descent endomorphisms
nodes.statement: In KPZ §3.4.5 assume G=Res_(K/F)H, p∤|π₁(G^der)|, classical H, x generic in its facet, no adjoint division factors of p-divisible degree, and the stated faithful minuscule product Hodge representation. For a Γ-stable Weyl lattice Λ̃ over a tame Galois splitting field K̃/K making x hyperspecial, the restricted integral representation is good. The full fixer is the intersection of the Weil-restricted split group with the centralizers of the Γ-actions t_γ and of multiplications t_a for O_F-algebra generators a of O_K̃. The comparison diagram with the invariant lattice chain (π̃^iΛ̃)^Γ and its total lattice has every arrow closed.

sources.match: Proves goodness, endomorphism cutout and the all-closed comparison diagram.

proofSteps: Use the integral descent equations to identify the group cutout.
Apply the stable Weyl-lattice comparison and the three polynomial closed embeddings.
After canonical model identification in LM.3, transfer these maps through normal full faithfulness. Check each arrow separately, including the Weil-split arrow.
acceptance: Commuting with Γ alone misses the O_K̃-linearity equations.

nodes.title: Good embeddings for acceptable Hodge data
nodes.statement: For p>2, an acceptable Hodge-type datum, p∤|π₁(G^der)|, and an R-smooth centralizer of a maximal breve-F-split torus, there is a good integral Hodge embedding 𝒢̃↪GL(Λ) into a single lattice, where 𝒢̃ is a stabilizer group scheme whose neutral component is the given parahoric 𝒢; the point may be moved within its facet and the representation replaced as in KZ Proposition 3.1.9. The construction may use a finite extension K/F that is not tame. The R-smooth centralizer and prime-to-p assumptions are retained. The step that the local-model map M^loc_(𝒢,μ)→M^loc_(𝒢_(K/F),μ_(K/F))⊗O_E is a closed immersion (KZ Lemma 3.1.10) is an open gap: its cited inputs give only a finite map that is a universal homeomorphism onto its image.

sources.match: Passes to a split extension and restricts back.

proofSteps: Request the R-smooth integral full-fixer embedding from the reductive-group integral representation continuation.
Pass to a field K over which G splits, obtain a good embedding of the Weil-restricted datum by the power-lattice embedding theorem, and restrict scalars.

The GS0 closed integral-Grassmannian map for the closed group embedding, together with normal full faithfulness, only gives a scheme map whose diamond is a closed immersion; such a map is the normalization of its schematic image (LM.3/normalization-of-image), as is FHLR Lemma 5.27’s finite universal homeomorphism onto the image.

By D10/uniqueness-of-integral-models(2) the composite to Gr(d,Λ)_(O_E) is a closed immersion exactly when the Zariski closure of G/P_μ there is normal with reduced special fibre. Supply this by a closed immersion on special fibres (the companion flag map on the admissible locus) followed by the Nakayama argument of PZ Proposition 8.1, or by proving the closure normal. Until then the closedness is the recorded gap.
acceptance: No p≥5 restriction is introduced, and no R-smoothness assumption is discarded.
A finite universal homeomorphism onto the image is not a closed immersion: the map to the Grassmannian is closed exactly when the image is normal.

nodes.title: Trace symplectic restriction of scalars
nodes.statement: For a finite separable extension K/F and a nondegenerate alternating K-bilinear form ψ on V, the F-form Ψ((v_i),(w_i))=Tr_(K/F)(Σ_i ψ(v_i,w_i)) on V^r is nondegenerate alternating. It yields the restriction-of-scalars symplectic embedding for the subgroup of the product similitude groups whose multipliers are one common element of F×. Independent K×-multipliers do not preserve a single F-similitude factor.

sources.match: Uses the trace of the direct-sum alternating form.

proofSteps: Alternation follows by trace linearity.
For nonzero v choose w with ψ(v,w)≠0, then scale w using nondegeneracy of the separable trace pairing.
The common F-multiplier pulls through the trace; test the absence of that common multiplier on a split product after scalar extension.
acceptance: For K=F and r=1 recover ψ exactly.

nodes.title: The one-lattice GL representative
nodes.statement: For GL(Λ) and minuscule μ=(1^d,0^(h−d)), the local-model v-sheaf is the diamond of the smooth projective Grassmannian of rank-d subspaces (equivalently rank-(h−d) quotients). With the SW quotient convention of rank d use the opposite flag Grassmannian of kernels of rank h−d. This supplies the GL case needed for normal schematic closure recovery.

sources.locator: Proposition 21.6.9 and proof of Corollary 21.6.10, pp. 201–203
sources.match: The B_dR⁺ kernel gives the closed map and flatness identifies its image.

proofSteps: Build the modification from the kernel of the universal quotient after B_dR⁺→R.
Use the integral Grassmannian closed-map criterion; its generic fibre is the minuscule flag.
Smoothness and flatness of the Grassmannian make its generic fibre schematically dense, so the image is exactly the v-closure.
acceptance: For h=3,d=1 distinguish P² of lines from the SW rank 1 quotient description by the duality dictionary.

nodes.title: The canonical model in the classical abelian-type range
nodes.statement: For standard data, split G^ad into factors on which μ^ad is nontrivial and trivial. Apply the auxiliary Hodge-cover construction to the first part and set M^can=M^pol_(𝒢′,μ′)⊗_(O_E′)O_E. This is a flat projective normal scheme with geometrically reduced special fibre, independent up to unique equivariant isomorphism of all auxiliary choices, and (M^can)^♦=M^v_(𝒢,μ). Its normal geometric special-fibre components are Cohen–Macaulay. The factors with trivial μ contribute the point; no hypothesis of nontrivial μ is imposed on the final theorem.

sources.match: Constructs the model and identifies its diamond.

proofSteps: Remove the μ-trivial adjoint factors and form the prime-to-p auxiliary closure.
The polynomial embedding theorem, proved before this identification, embeds it into the ordinary GL Grassmannian.
Invoke the existing D10 normal-closure recovery theorem using GS0’s closed integral-Grassmannian map and the proved GL case.
Apply the imported minuscule central-surjection and connected-level comparisons, then normal full faithfulness, to obtain the canonical model and uniqueness.
acceptance: The proof order is polynomial embeddings → normal recovery → canonical representability.

uses.how: Supplies the local-model locus in the lattice criterion.
Supplies the special fibre whose tangent spaces are studied.

nodes.title: Integral Hodge maps and normalizations of images
nodes.statement: For a standard datum and any integral Hodge embedding, the functorial scheme map M^can→Gr(d,Λ)_(O_E) identifies M^can with the normalization of its schematic image. Goodness is the stronger assertion that this map is already a closed immersion. The diagram of geometric special-fibre points with the Witt Grassmannians commutes.

sources.match: States the normalization and geometric point diagram.

proofSteps: Construct the diamond map and lift it by proper normal full faithfulness.
Use generic closed immersion, properness and geometric-fibre injectivity to get a finite birational map onto the image.
Normality of the source gives the normalization; identify the point map by specialization functoriality.
acceptance: Normalizing an image is not the same statement as image normality.

nodes.title: Algebraic and Witt special-fibre interfaces
nodes.statement: In the quasi-tame prime-to-p polynomial range, the special fibre is the reduced μ-admissible union in the equal-characteristic companion partial affine flag, with Bruhat closure relations. Its perfection identifies with the μ-admissible locus in the Witt flag. For a general bound and arbitrary parahoric G over a p-adic field, the reduced v-special fibre of M^v is A_(𝒢,μ)^♦. These are two comparisons with a common perfected object, not a canonical identification of every unperfected equal-characteristic flag with a Witt flag.

sources.match: Uses the equal-characteristic special-fibre realization.
Identifies the reduced special v-fibre for arbitrary bounds.

proofSteps: For polynomial models use the reduced special-fibre theorem and the companion root data.
For the general v-bound, specialize extremal strata for one inclusion; use nonzero nearby-cycle stalks and constant terms to exclude additional maximal strata.
Record the descent of the perfection comparison with its Frobenius action.
acceptance: Keep generic flag, companion special scheme, perfected Witt locus and v-special fibre in different types.

nodes.title: General-bound local-model kimberlites
nodes.statement: For any connected reductive group over a p-adic field, parahoric level and dominant bound μ, M^v is a flat proper π-adic kimberlite; (M^v,Gr_≤μ) is rich smelted. Its reduction is the perfectly finite-type admissible locus and specialization is surjective. Apply the existing D11 proper-kimberlite criterion and verify its density, formalization of C-valued sections, and spatial generic-fibre hypotheses explicitly. No tangent or minuscule condition is used.

sources.locator: Proposition 4.14 and Remark 4.15, pp. 30–31; Theorem 6.16, pp. 39–40
sources.match: Establishes the kimberlite and special-fibre properties.

Records M as a kimberlite whose reduced special fibre is the admissible locus, and uses the tubes of the pair (M×Spd O_F, Gr_μ×Spd F); richness of that pair is planned here through the D11 criterion, not quoted from GLX.

proofSteps: Use the bounded integral Grassmannian properness and generic density to verify the proper criterion.
Formalize geometric generic points by the extension property of bounded modifications.
Identify the reduction by the preceding comparison; perfect finite type gives the local noetherian and cJ finiteness used for richness.
acceptance: Specialization onto a nonempty closed stratum is surjective even for a nonminuscule bound.

nodes.title: General minuscule weak normal representability
nodes.statement: For any connected reductive G over F finite over Q_p, any parahoric 𝒢 and minuscule μ, there is a unique flat projective weakly normal O_E-model M^wn of G/P_μ, with a specified equivariant diamond isomorphism (M^wn)^♦≅M^v. No p≥5, tame or abelian-type restriction is present. This theorem stops at weak normality; LM.7 proves normality and geometrically reduced special fibre.

sources.match: Proves representability via Iwahori comparison, descent and weak normalization.

proofSteps: In the polynomial-lift range compare generic and special fibres and their specialization maps at Iwahori level, using AGLR7.13,7.19–7.21 and the D11 triple theorem.
Descend through the Iwahori-to-parahoric v-cover; compare the actual closed equivalence relations on both sides.

For arbitrary G embed into a Weil-restricted split group and take the absolute weak normalization of the flat flag closure in its scheme model. The precise integral-lift and finite weak-normalization contracts remain supplier gaps.
acceptance: This intermediate theorem must not use the final tube normality theorem in its proof.

nodes.title: Formal-curve tangent span
nodes.statement: For a finite-type k-scheme X and k-point x, let C_(X,x) be the set of pointed k-morphisms γ:Spec k[[a]]→X taking the closed point to x. Define T^cur_x X as the k-submodule of the existing Zariski tangent space T_xX generated by dγ(∂/∂a) for γ∈C_(X,x). Curve-spanned means T^cur_x X=T_xX. This does not mean every vector is the derivative of one formal curve. The light module interface takes a family of derivative vectors and forms Submodule.span k of its range.

sources.match: Introduces the curve span and its distinction from ambient tangent spaces.

proofSteps: Use the existing scheme tangent space and the requested tangent functor on pointed morphisms.
Generate a submodule by the derivative family; functoriality follows from the tangent chain rule.
acceptance: A union of derivative directions can span a plane without every plane vector lying on a curve.

nodes.title: Reduced tangent cones and a curve obstruction
nodes.statement: For X finite type over k, x rational, every nonzero derivative of a pointed formal curve is a k-point of the reduced tangent cone in T_xX. Thus curve spanning implies that the reduced-cone k-points span T_xX. For X: x²+xyz=0 at the origin, T₀X=k³ and T^cur₀X={x=0}; this X is reduced and reducible, not normal.

For the example, if (f,g,h) is a curve then f(f+gh)=0 in the domain k[[a]], so f=0 or f=−gh∈(a²).
The y- and z-axes show that all of the plane x=0 lies in the span.
acceptance: The origin has tangent dimension 3 and curve-span dimension 2.

nodes.title: Big-cell tangent coordinates and weights
nodes.statement: Let k be algebraically closed of characteristic p>2, G split reductive, T⊂B a split pair and λ dominant. At t^λ the translated negative big cell t^λL^{--}G t^(−λ) gives an open chart of Gr_G. With a Chevalley basis, the tangent is the direct sum over roots α of t^(〈λ,α〉−1)k[t^(−1)]X_α and the Cartan term t^(−1)k[t^(−1)]Lie(T). Rotation×T acts with the corresponding affine-root weights; the tangent of S_μ and its curve span are stable subspaces with these weight decompositions.

sources.match: Uses the negative big cell and root/Cartan tangent decomposition.

proofSteps: Import the algebraic loop big-cell chart, not the diamond flag chart of GS0.
Differentiate the root subgroup coordinates and torus loop coordinates at the identity and conjugate by t^λ.
Use torus diagonalizability to project the curve span onto weights; a projection belongs to a span, not necessarily to a single curve.
acceptance: The exponent for x_α(t^(−j)a) after translation is 〈λ,α〉−j.

nodes.title: Mod-p abelian cocharacters and minuscule tests
nodes.statement: For split classical adjoint-simple root data use Bourbaki labels. A dominant coweight is of mod-p abelian type when: in A it is any sum of dominant minuscule coweights; in B or C it is a nonnegative multiple of the unique minuscule coweight; in D^R it is rω₁∨; in D^H it is sω_(n−1)∨+tω_n∨, r,s,t≥0. For products require this factorwise. The finite minuscule test-weight sets are S_A={all fundamental weights}, S_B={ω_n}, S_C={ω₁}, S_(D^R)={ω_(n−1),ω_n}, S_(D^H)={ω₁,ω_(n−1),ω_n}; tests are on the simply connected derived cover, not necessarily characters of the original adjoint group.

sources.match: Gives the classical cocharacter types and test-weight sets.

proofSteps: Import finite root data, their Bourbaki coordinates and the simply connected weight lattice.
Bundle the permitted cocharacter family and type-dependent finite test set.
Apply the prime-to-p derived central-isogeny tangent comparison before using test representations unavailable on G itself.
acceptance: B and C exchange the coweight and weight roles; test the listed spin and standard weights.

nodes.title: Finkelberg–Mirković representation bounds
nodes.statement: Let G be split connected reductive over the algebraically closed field k, and for a dominant weight ν∈X^*(T)^+ let V(ν)=Ind_B^G(−w₀ν)^* be the Weyl module. For an R-point (𝓔,φ) of Gr_G put 𝓔(ν)=𝓔×^G V(ν), and let 𝓔⁰(ν) be the bundle of the trivial torsor. The point lies in S^FM_μ when t^〈μ,−w₀ν〉φ(𝓔(ν))⊂𝓔⁰(ν)⊂t^〈μ,−ν〉φ(𝓔(ν)) inside 𝓔(ν)[1/t] for every dominant ν. Both inclusions are imposed. S^FM_μ is a closed projective subscheme of Gr_G containing S_μ, so T_(t^λ)S_μ⊂T_(t^λ)S^FM_μ. Neither equality of schemes nor reducedness of the FM bound is assumed in characteristic p. The reduction to G^der simply connected is made in the theorems that use the bound.

sources.match: Defines the two lattice bounds and projectivity.

Equal R-ranks of adjacent quotients are not enough. The polarized version includes an invertible R-module L and antisymmetric dualities M_Λ≅Hom_R(M_(Λ*),L) compatible with transition and periodicity. nodes.statement: For any reductive G/F over a p-adic field, parahoric 𝒢 and geometric dominant μ, every geometric tube of M^v is connected. Equivalently its rich smelted pair is topologically normal. There is no tameness, minuscule, classical-type or residue-characteristic restriction. For breve E⊆F′⊆C_p the GLX base-changed local-model pair has the same property.

proofSteps: Reduce to Iwahori level: Demazure resolutions show fibres of the admissible projection connected, all containing the minimal coset representative; use the D11 tube-transfer criterion.
A disconnected tube gives, by algebraicity of RΨIC and the general comparison, a clopen splitting over a connected étale neighbourhood U.
Its codimension≤1 open W is connected by S₂ and its tubes are connected by the stalk calculation, so all of the tube over W lies in one clopen piece.
The other piece yields a nonzero perverse direct summand supported in codimension≥2 whose degree−d cohomology is nonzero, contradicting the perverse support bound.
Use the geometric tube definition to descend the assertion to the GLX intermediate base fields.

nodes.title: General normal minuscule local models
nodes.statement: For every connected reductive G/F, F finite over Q_p, parahoric level and minuscule μ, the weakly normal representative is normal, flat and projective over O_E, with geometrically reduced special fibre and generic flag G/P_μ; its diamond is M^v. Work after completing with algebraically closed residue field when applying the D11 normality-via-tubes criterion, then descend. No p≥5 or tame hypothesis is present. Cohen–Macaulayness or Frobenius splitting in all cases is not included in this theorem.

Apply proper normal full faithfulness for uniqueness and equivariance.

nodes.title: Local-model nearby cycles and monodromy
nodes.statement: In the tame Pappas–Zhu polynomial-model range, take the scheme-theoretic ℓ-adic nearby cycles of the generic IC sheaf, with ℓ≠p. Inertia of a splitting extension acts unipotently. At a very special vertex it acts trivially. These assertions concern splitting-field inertia; they do not assert that full reflex-field inertia always acts trivially. Minuscule generic IC is Q_ℓ[d](d/2), with the Tate-root convention fixed in the trace dictionary.

proofSteps: Pass to a splitting extension and to Iwahori level, using proper pushforward compatibility with the unipotent/non-unipotent decomposition.
Proper base change computes the cohomology as split Schubert IC cohomology, with trivial splitting-field inertia.
Centrality gives Wakimoto filtrations and faithfulness of the associated cohomology to kill the non-unipotent summand.
At a very special vertex the semisimple Satake category has faithful cohomology, so the entire splitting-field inertia action is trivial.

nodes.title: The local-model semisimple trace function
nodes.statement: For a finite residue extension F_q/k_E define φ_q(x)=Σ_i(−1)^i Tr^ss(Fr_q,H^i(RΨ Q_ℓ)_x), using geometric Frobenius. For an inertia-admissible filtration, Tr^ss is the sum of traces on the inertia invariants of its graded pieces; it is independent of that filtration. Extend φ_q by 0 along the companion-model embedding into G′(F_q((t)))/P′. Normalize Haar measure so vol(P′)=1. This yields a compactly supported P′-bi-invariant function. Fix q^(1/2) and Tate convention so Q_ℓ(1) has Frobenius q^(−1).

Then φ_q=q^(d/2)z_(μ,q). The companion and mixed-characteristic coset bijection gives the corresponding function on G(E_r). proposal.title: Geometric Satake, Part II: the rational Gelfand proof
proposal.brief: Starting from GS0 Witt Grassmannians and GS2 convolution, plan equivariant cohomology as an R_G-bimodule, equivariant Künneth and equality of left/right actions; descend monoidality to ordinary cohomology. Build the finite-level opposite Grassmannian IC correspondence, pinned opposition and normalized IC involution, checking stalk/costalk and open-orbit maps. Use the rational KL/stalk sign comparison and the costalk filtration to identify the global cohomology involution and its graded phase. Construct the rational commutativity constraint and prove involutivity, the symmetry and hexagon with the normalized sign, retaining half-degree/Tate conventions. Coefficients are characteristic-zero rational ℓ-adic, not an integral or mod-ℓ extension. Import finite Weyl twisted-involution identities from the root/Coxeter owner, cohomology/perversity from EDC and GS0, and flag geometry from the shared early prefix. Tests must include the unit, a minuscule GL₂ orbit, convolution associativity/opposite reversal and the odd-degree sign. Collate Zhu’s published pp. 439–468, §§2.2–2.4 and the relevant Lusztig–Yun arguments; route all source findings already attached to these 29 items. This is a complete design brief, not a local-model proof claim.

restructure.detail: Make GS0’s early algebraic loop prefix the unique owner of arbitrary-field affine Grassmannians, twisted parahoric flags, their common Schubert/Demazure geometry and polynomial BD criteria. GS.1 and ET.2b import that prefix. Their global-curve and Hitchin constructions stay with their existing owners; LM only plans local-model closures and applications.

D11 owns general tube cohomology GL4.7 before GS2. GS2 owns the early centrality/perversity/Wakimoto prefix ALWY4.12–4.19. LM.7 owns only the local-model stalk application and connected-tubes proof. Neither D11 nor the early GS2 theorem may consume LM.7.

Add a continuation above the existing building/parahoric roadmap for generic classical minuscule Hodge covers, stable integral Weyl lattices, polynomial lifts of toral representations, symplectic building factorization, R-smooth full-fixer embeddings and their descent. The current RG2 objects and theorem scope remain unchanged.

Finite invariant folding is already supplied and is imported. Propose the separate modular minuscule dominance/root-string and Cartan coefficient direction named in the gap; do not add it silently to the accepted folding packet.

Extend the existing scheme/descent foundations in its own direction with finite relative Grassmannian representability, finite and weak normalization, the flat-DVR normality and reducedness criteria, Serre/depth and canonical-module connectedness, and pointed tangent functoriality on the existing Tau Ceti carrier. Import existing scheme morphisms and descent; do not claim the current SF0 targets already supply these stronger contracts.

Extend global good-prime PEL data by local semisimple Q_p-algebras and involutions, ramified orders, periodic lattice index data and their trace dualities. Import existing determinant polynomial laws when their hypotheses apply. LM.6 retains the module-chain forms, naive local-model quotient functor and Drinfeld comparisons; no global PEL moduli or abelian scheme is replanned.

Build parahoric Bernstein centers and compatible idempotent changes of level above the existing Hecke and spherical Satake layers. Its endpoint is the normalized center-to-spherical isomorphism, with no local-model or Shimura trace formula as a premise.

review.notes: Independent review by Claude (session claude-iW3aXv). All 15 sources were opened at every node locator: the 14 public PDFs (SHA-256 matching the packet) and the cleared Scholze–Weinstein copy read in place. All 60 nodes checked: 39 verified, 21 corrected, none added. All 5 baseline declarations confirmed at Mathlib 082e2d3 and Tau Ceti f790474; the 17 cross-roadmap node prerequisites were read in their accepted packets. Main corrections: LM.7/acceptable-good-embedding planned closedness of the Weil-restriction local-model map by a route that only yields the normalization of the image, so the closedness is now a recorded gap; the FM bound and PEL chain definitions were restated faithfully (a rank-only chain condition would admit wrong objects); KP Proposition 2.2.4’s prime-to-p hypothesis was restored; 16 source locators were corrected. Source issues: all 12 confirmed (E4 locator and E6 correction revised) and two added (E13: KPZ Proposition 4.3.10 needs p≠2; E14: a q-exponent sign misprint in PZ v4 §9.d.3). The suggested file gained two statements and elaborates at the pins with twelve proof-placeholder warnings and nothing else. Every stage stays planned, none closed; 13 gaps and 15 requests remain.
